newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH ZLOTY FLAT VS BASKET, NBP-BILL YIELD RISES.
newsitem.headline: POLISH ZLOTY FLAT VS BASKET, NBP-BILL YIELD RISES.

text.p: The Polish zloty closed flat against the currency basket after a small intraday fall caused by domestic client orders and speculation under dollar/mark moves before the U.S. Federal Reserve meeting later today.

"After some early domestic client dollar-buying the zloty regained morning losses in the afternoon...and the unit should drift between 2.9 and 3.0 percent from parity for the next several days," said Tomasz Nowakowski from Bank Handlowy SA.
Analysts expect the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee to announce an increase of its key Funds rate by 25 basis points after its meeting ends around 1915 GMT.
The zloty closed at 3.03/3.02 percent from the trading band centre, flat from Monday's close at 3.05/3.00 percent after hitting intraday lows around 2.9 percent from parity.
It closed at 3.0785/93 to the dollar, up from 3.0815/30 on Monday and at 1.8240/49 to the mark, down from 1.8230/40.

Dealers said foreign investors who purchased Polish T-bills on Monday already made forex transactions while longer term investors, who had bought bonds over the last several months, remained on the sidelines on Tuesday.
On the money market one-day rates eased as banks found cash after sqaring monthly reserve accounts, dealers said.
Overnight rates closed at 22.40/22.80 percent, down from opening's 22.75/22.95 while tomorrow/next rates were at 22.50/22.80 percent, also down from 22.70/22.95.
Dealers said that one-day rates should not rise above 23 percent for the remainder of the March reserve -- which ends during the Easter holiday break on Monday.
The central bank increased the average yield on its 91-day NBP-bill to 22.15 percent from 22.00 percent after it increased its main 14-day drainage rate also to 22.15 percent last week.
Dealers said the move was in line with the bank's policy to keep market rates high to curb consumer credit action.
"The central bank is keeping high market rates to curb credit and with it domestic demand in order to keep the trade deficit from widening too quickly," said Marcin Dec, dealer at Bank Gdanski SA.
Dealers said today's move was expected by the market but some thought that NBP-bill yields would rise further.
At the auction the central bank sold 138 million zlotys of the bills, while rejecting bids worth 255 million zlotys.
